title: Interactive Cross-modal Learning for Text-3D Scene Retrieval

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper claims to encapsulate features in a minimum enclosing hypersphere, but the constraint is written as u_i^j o_i^T <= R_i, which is a linear half-space constraint, not the usual squared distance constraint (||u_i^j - o_i||^2 <= R_i^2) of a hypersphere. This misrepresents the geometry and invalidates the subsequent boundary/central set definitions.

Both loss terms use the raw similarity score S (e.g., dot product or cosine similarity) inside a log loss: log S in Eq.(7) and log(1 - S) in Eq.(9). Cosine similarity can be negative, making log undefined; similarity can also be exactly 1, making log(0) undefined. The losses require a probability or strictly positive bounded measure, but S is not constrained as such.

In Table 2, the RoMa baseline numbers (ScanRefer R@1=9.7, R@5=33.1, R@10=50.2, Rsum=93.0) exactly duplicate the VSE∞ row above. This contradicts Table 1, where RoMa with coarse descriptions has different values (11.4, 34.8, 54.4, 100.6). The row appears to be a copy-paste error.

Figure 4 shows approximate R@1 values: for ScanRefer fine-grained at round 5 ~39, but Table 1 reports IDeal† R@1=37.8; for coarse-grained round 5 ~15, but Table 1 reports 12.8. The per-round values in the figure do not match the final reported results, indicating a discrepancy.

The paper cites [60] Zhang, L., Wang, M., & Liu, Q. (2022). Bayesian Density Correction for Cross-Modal Retrieval. In Proceedings of ICLR 2022, as the theoretical foundation for the density correction. ICLR 2022 proceedings contain no such paper, and the title is suspiciously generic; the citation appears to be fabricated to lend credibility to the ad-hoc density compensation.
